question: Why did net sales change between August and September 2026?

report.summary: Net sales decreased by 8500 cents, from 191500 cents in August 2026 to 183000 cents in September 2026. Gross sales increased by 10000 cents, but refunds increased by 18500 cents, so the refund increase more than offset the sales growth. The small segment drove most of the decline: its net sales fell by 7500 cents, compared with a 1000-cent decline for the large segment.

findings.statement: Overall August net sales were 191500 cents and September net sales were 183000 cents. August gross sales and refunds were 194000 cents and 2500 cents; September gross sales and refunds were 204000 cents and 21000 cents.
The small segment's net sales fell from 56500 cents in August to 49000 cents in September. Its gross sales rose from 59000 cents to 65000 cents, but refunds rose from 2500 cents to 16000 cents.
The large segment's net sales fell from 135000 cents in August to 134000 cents in September. Its gross sales rose from 135000 cents to 139000 cents, while refunds rose from 0 cents to 5000 cents.
The available data records refund amounts and dates, but not refund reasons, so it cannot establish why refunds increased.

assumptions: August is 2026-08-01 inclusive through 2026-09-01 exclusive; September is 2026-09-01 inclusive through 2026-10-01 exclusive.
Gross sales are grouped by order date and refunds by refund date.
Refunds are assigned to the segment of the customer on the original order.
Dates are interpreted as UTC date strings.
open_questions: Which individual orders and refund records account for the September increase?
What caused the increased refunds? Additional refund reason or customer-support data would be needed.

queries.purpose: Compare August and September gross sales, refunds, and net sales overall and by customer segment.
queries.sql: WITH periods AS (SELECT '2026-08-01' AS start_date, '2026-09-01' AS end_date, 'August 2026' AS period UNION ALL SELECT '2026-09-01','2026-10-01','September 2026'), gross AS (SELECT p.period,c.segment,SUM(o.amount_cents) AS gross FROM periods p JOIN orders o ON o.order_date>=p.start_date AND o.order_date<p.end_date JOIN customers c ON c.customer_id=o.customer_id GROUP BY p.period,c.segment), refunds_by_segment AS (SELECT p.period,c.segment,SUM(r.amount_cents) AS refunds FROM periods p JOIN refunds r ON r.refund_date>=p.start_date AND r.refund_date<p.end_date JOIN orders o ON o.order_id=r.order_id JOIN customers c ON c.customer_id=o.customer_id GROUP BY p.period,c.segment), segs AS (SELECT segment FROM customers GROUP BY segment), all_values AS (SELECT p.period,s.segment FROM periods p CROSS JOIN segs s) SELECT v.period,v.segment,COALESCE(g.gross,0) AS gross,COALESCE(r.refunds,0) AS refunds,COALESCE(g.gross,0)-COALESCE(r.refunds,0) AS net FROM all_values v LEFT JOIN gross g ON g.period=v.period AND g.segment=v.segment LEFT JOIN refunds_by_segment r ON r.period=v.period AND r.segment=v.segment UNION ALL SELECT p.period,'ALL',COALESCE((SELECT SUM(amount_cents) FROM orders o WHERE o.order_date>=p.start_date AND o.order_date<p.end_date),0),COALESCE((SELECT SUM(r.amount_cents) FROM refunds r WHERE r.refund_date>=p.start_date AND r.refund_date<p.end_date),0),COALESCE((SELECT SUM(amount_cents) FROM orders o WHERE o.order_date>=p.start_date AND o.order_date<p.end_date),0)-COALESCE((SELECT SUM(r.amount_cents) FROM refunds r WHERE r.refund_date>=p.start_date AND r.refund_date<p.end_date),0) FROM periods p ORDER BY period,segment;

queries.sql: WITH periods AS (SELECT '2026-08-01' start_date,'2026-09-01' end_date,'August 2026' period UNION ALL SELECT '2026-09-01','2026-10-01','September 2026'), gross AS (SELECT p.period,c.segment,SUM(o.amount_cents) gross FROM periods p JOIN orders o ON o.order_date>=p.start_date AND o.order_date<p.end_date JOIN customers c ON c.customer_id=o.customer_id GROUP BY p.period,c.segment), rb AS (SELECT p.period,c.segment,SUM(r.amount_cents) refunds FROM periods p JOIN refunds r ON r.refund_date>=p.start_date AND r.refund_date<p.end_date JOIN orders o ON o.order_id=r.order_id JOIN customers c ON c.customer_id=o.customer_id GROUP BY p.period,c.segment), segs AS (SELECT DISTINCT segment FROM customers), x AS (SELECT p.period,s.segment FROM periods p CROSS JOIN segs s), detail AS (SELECT x.period,x.segment,COALESCE(g.gross,0) gross,COALESCE(rb.refunds,0) refunds,COALESCE(g.gross,0)-COALESCE(rb.refunds,0) net FROM x LEFT JOIN gross g USING(period,segment) LEFT JOIN rb USING(period,segment)), totals AS (SELECT p.period,'ALL' segment,COALESCE((SELECT SUM(amount_cents) FROM orders o WHERE o.order_date>=p.start_date AND o.order_date<p.end_date),0) gross,COALESCE((SELECT SUM(amount_cents) FROM refunds r WHERE r.refund_date>=p.start_date AND r.refund_date<p.end_date),0) refunds FROM periods p) SELECT period,segment,gross,refunds,gross-refunds net FROM (SELECT * FROM detail UNION ALL SELECT period,segment,gross,refunds FROM totals) ORDER BY period,segment;

queries.purpose: Quantify the August-to-September changes in gross sales, refunds, and net sales by segment.
queries.sql: WITH q AS (SELECT * FROM (VALUES ('August 2026','ALL',194000,2500,191500),('August 2026','large',135000,0,135000),('August 2026','small',59000,2500,56500),('September 2026','ALL',204000,21000,183000),('September 2026','large',139000,5000,134000),('September 2026','small',65000,16000,49000)) AS t(period,segment,gross,refunds,net)) SELECT a.segment,b.gross-a.gross gross_change,b.refunds-a.refunds refunds_change,b.net-a.net net_change FROM q a JOIN q b ON a.segment=b.segment WHERE a.period='August 2026' AND b.period='September 2026';

queries.purpose: Reconfirm August and September totals and segment breakdown used to explain the net sales change.
queries.sql: WITH p(period,s,e) AS (VALUES ('August 2026','2026-08-01','2026-09-01'),('September 2026','2026-09-01','2026-10-01')), o AS (SELECT p.period,c.segment,SUM(amount_cents) gross FROM p JOIN orders x ON x.order_date>=p.s AND x.order_date<p.e JOIN customers c ON c.customer_id=x.customer_id GROUP BY p.period,c.segment), r AS (SELECT p.period,c.segment,SUM(f.amount_cents) refunds FROM p JOIN refunds f ON f.refund_date>=p.s AND f.refund_date<p.e JOIN orders x ON x.order_id=f.order_id JOIN customers c ON c.customer_id=x.customer_id GROUP BY p.period,c.segment) SELECT p.period,COALESCE(o.segment,r.segment) segment,COALESCE(o.gross,0) gross,COALESCE(r.refunds,0) refunds,COALESCE(o.gross,0)-COALESCE(r.refunds,0) net FROM p LEFT JOIN o ON o.period=p.period LEFT JOIN r ON r.period=p.period AND r.segment=o.segment ORDER BY p.period,segment;

You investigate questions about a fictional company's sales with read-only SQL over a small SQLite database.

## How to work

1. Call `run_sql` for a first look. Compute every figure in SQL, not in your head.
2. Read the result, then choose at least one follow-up query based on it, for example separating gross sales from refunds or comparing customer segments.
3. You have at most 6 query attempts, and errors count. Two to four queries are usually enough.
4. Call `submit_report` once the results answer the question.

## Metric rules in SQL

- Apply the business rules below even where they differ from the usual meaning of a metric name.
- Use half-open periods: `order_date >= '2026-08-01' AND order_date < '2026-09-01'`. Filter refunds by `refund_date`, never by the date of their order.
- Aggregate orders and refunds in separate subqueries, then combine them. Joining refund rows to orders repeats order amounts.
- A refund's segment is the segment of the customer on its original order: refunds → orders → customers.

## Report

- Every figure in `metrics` must appear exactly as a cell in the result of the query it cites, for example `q2`. Query any total or segment figure you need.
- In text, write money only as an integer followed by "cents", for example "183000 cents". Do not use "$" or dollars; the application formats money.
- `observed`: shown directly by a query result. `inferred`: a conclusion drawn from observed figures. `unknown`: something the data cannot establish. Refund rows record amounts and dates, not why customers asked for refunds, so do not guess causes.
- State the periods, units and any other assumption. If the question does not name periods, choose them from the data and say so.

# Business data investigation: exercise rules

These fictional rules are the source of truth for this assignment. No industry research is required.

1. Use customers, orders, and refunds. IDs link refunds to orders and orders to customers; one order can have multiple refunds.
2. Gross sales for a period sum orders by order_date. Refunds for that period sum refunds by refund_date. Net sales equal gross sales minus refunds. Use UTC dates and half-open periods: start included, end excluded.
3. Use integer USD cents. Group order and refund totals separately before combining them; joining raw refund rows to orders can repeat order amounts.
4. Assign refunds to the segment of the customer on the original order. The records show amounts and dates, not why a customer requested a refund.

## Schema

```sql
CREATE TABLE customers (customer_id TEXT PRIMARY KEY, segment TEXT NOT NULL);
CREATE TABLE orders (order_id TEXT PRIMARY KEY, customer_id TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES customers(customer_id), order_date TEXT NOT NULL, amount_cents INTEGER NOT NULL CHECK(amount_cents >= 0));
CREATE TABLE refunds (refund_id TEXT PRIMARY KEY, order_id TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES orders(order_id), refund_date TEXT NOT NULL, amount_cents INTEGER NOT NULL CHECK(amount_cents >= 0));
```
Why did net sales change between August and September 2026?

function.arguments: {"purpose":"Compare August and September gross sales, refunds, and net sales overall and by customer segment.","sql":"WITH periods AS (SELECT '2026-08-01' AS start_date, '2026-09-01' AS end_date, 'August 2026' AS period UNION ALL SELECT '2026-09-01','2026-10-01','September 2026'), gross AS (SELECT p.period,c.segment,SUM(o.amount_cents) AS gross FROM periods p JOIN orders o ON o.order_date>=p.start_date AND o.order_date<p.end_date JOIN customers c ON c.customer_id=o.customer_id GROUP BY p.period,c.segment), refunds_by_segment AS (SELECT p.period,c.segment,SUM(r.amount_cents) AS refunds FROM periods p JOIN refunds r ON r.refund_date>=p.start_date AND r.refund_date<p.end_date JOIN orders o ON o.order_id=r.order_id JOIN customers c ON c.customer_id=o.customer_id GROUP BY p.period,c.segment), segs AS (SELECT segment FROM customers GROUP BY segment), all_values AS (SELECT p.period,s.segment FROM periods p CROSS JOIN segs s) SELECT v.period,v.segment,COALESCE(g.gross,0) AS gross,COALESCE(r.refunds,0) AS refunds,COALESCE(g.gross,0)-COALESCE(r.refunds,0) AS net FROM all_values v LEFT JOIN gross g ON g.period=v.period AND g.segment=v.segment LEFT JOIN refunds_by_segment r ON r.period=v.period AND r.segment=v.segment UNION ALL SELECT p.period,'ALL',COALESCE((SELECT SUM(amount_cents) FROM orders o WHERE o.order_date>=p.start_date AND o.order_date<p.end_date),0),COALESCE((SELECT SUM(r.amount_cents) FROM refunds r WHERE r.refund_date>=p.start_date AND r.refund_date<p.end_date),0),COALESCE((SELECT SUM(amount_cents) FROM orders o WHERE o.order_date>=p.start_date AND o.order_date<p.end_date),0)-COALESCE((SELECT SUM(r.amount_cents) FROM refunds r WHERE r.refund_date>=p.start_date AND r.refund_date<p.end_date),0) FROM periods p ORDER BY period,segment;"}
